I closed all 8 rows. Three were flaky-or-order-dependent, two were flaky, and the other three, plus the double 9.03, were stale belt checks I retired. I re-ran each check with `runchk.sh` under the lock. The fixture edits are in one commit, `ac3d4b4e`. Nothing needed a game change, so no mk-cw script or ship was used.

| Version | Verdict | What I did | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17.75 | Order dependent | The pause legend depends on state: in the hub it says "use a station". The check read it before entering the raid, so I moved the read inside the raid, as 18.25 does. | Failed first in a fresh tab, passed 3 times after the fix |
| 9.93 | Flaky | No change | Passed 3 times alone |
| 9.92 | Flaky | No change | Passed 3 times alone |
| 10.68 | Flaky | The rarity roll can turn the carbine into `carbine_v`, so the check now accepts the plain id or the `_v` id in both arms. | Passed 3 times before the edit and 2 times after. The failure is a random roll, so those runs only show it still passes. |
| 9.03 (both checks) | Stale | Retired: `SKIP: removed by his order`. The wheel dimming of a spent item type is covered by 26.33. | SKIP confirmed |
| 9.31 | Stale | Retired with the same SKIP (items no longer go on the bar). | SKIP confirmed |
| 11.60 | Stale | Retired with the same SKIP. A frag is used from the wheel, and the wheel counts are tested by the 26.xx checks. | SKIP confirmed |
| 23.95 | Stale | Retired with the same SKIP (the wheel has fixed eight slots). | SKIP confirmed |

For 9.03, 11.60 and 23.95 the SKIP text names his order. I did not write new wheel checks, because the 26.xx checks already cover the wheel side.

All 8 rows in `corpus-triage.md` are now marked DONE.

TASK DONE
